**Option 2: Request Permission Override**

<details>
<summary>🛡️ Learn more about this security feature</summary>

- Executing malicious code on the deployment server

- Potentially compromising the infrastructure

Preview deployments are powerful but require trust. Only users with repository write access can trigger them.
</details>

[reviewer-agent] Ready: No blocking findings in the current diff.

The updated `TC-SEC-004` test now covers the real UI path instead of the old simplified API-only contract, and the new helper usage stays within the QA guide expectations: tenant-scoped fixture setup, cleanup in `afterAll`, no seeded data dependency, no per-test retry overrides, and selectors that match the current security UI implementation.

I confirmed the targeted gap is closed in spec coverage under the enterprise-enabled discovery mode used for these tests: `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=1 yarn test:integration:spec-coverage` reports `SEC: scenarios 7/7, tests 8, coverage 100.00%`, and `TC-SEC-004` is no longer listed as uncovered.

Residual risk: I did not boot a fresh ephemeral app to rerun the full passkey browser flow end-to-end in this review turn. My review used the branch diff, source/selector alignment, existing Playwright artifacts, and the scoped spec-coverage check.

[reviewer-agent] Ready: no blocking issues found in the current HCK-0050 changes.

Under the relevant enterprise-security profile, `OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES=1 OM_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_MODULES_SECURITY=1 yarn test:integration:spec-coverage --json` now reports `SEC` scenario coverage at `7/7`, and `TC-SEC-004` is no longer in `uncoveredScenarioIds`. The updated [TC-SEC-004.spec.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0050/packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/TC-SEC-004.spec.ts:1) also matches the scenario and QA-guide requirements more closely by using real UI flow coverage and a scenario source comment, while [securityFixtures.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0050/packages/enterprise/src/modules/security/__integration__/helpers/securityFixtures.ts:1) moves shared API helper imports onto the preferred `@open-mercato/core/helpers/integration/*` path.

Residual risk: the preserved `.ai/qa/test-results/results.json` only shows this spec as skipped in the recorded run, and I could not rerun the live spec here because Docker CLI is unavailable for ephemeral startup and no local app was running on `http://localhost:3000`. That is a verification gap, not a branch defect.
